struct State<'o, 'input, 'arena> {
    options: &'o ConvertShapeToPath,
    implicated: Implicated<'input, 'arena>,
    plain_targets: HashMap<&'static str, HashSet<oxvg_ast::element::HashableElement<'input, 'arena>>>,
}

impl<'input, 'arena> Visitor<'input, 'arena> for State<'_, 'input, 'arena> {
    type Error = JobsError<'input>;

    fn is_plain_protected(&self, element: &Element<'input, 'arena>) -> bool {
        let name = match element.qual_name() {
            ElementId::Rect => "rect",
            ElementId::Line => "line",
            ElementId::Polyline => "polyline",
            ElementId::Polygon => "polygon",
            ElementId::Circle => "circle",
            ElementId::Ellipse => "ellipse",
            _ => return false,
        };
        self.plain_targets
            .get(name)
            .is_some_and(|targets| targets.contains(&oxvg_ast::element::HashableElement::new(element.clone())))
    }

    fn element(
        &self,
        element: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
        context: &mut Context<'input, 'arena, '_>,
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let name = element.qual_name();

        let options = &self.options;
        let path_options = &convert::Options {
            precision: options.float_precision.0,
            ..convert::Options::default()
        };
        let convert_arcs = options.convert_arcs;

        match name {
            ElementId::Rect if !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) => {
                ConvertShapeToPath::rect_to_path(element, path_options, context.info);
            }
            ElementId::Line if !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) => {
                ConvertShapeToPath::line_to_path(element, path_options, context.info);
            }
            ElementId::Polyline if !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) => {
                ConvertShapeToPath::poly_to_path(element, path_options, false, context.info);
            }
            ElementId::Polygon if !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) => {
                ConvertShapeToPath::poly_to_path(element, path_options, true, context.info);
            }
            ElementId::Circle
                if convert_arcs && !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) =>
            {
                ConvertShapeToPath::circle_to_path(element, path_options, context.info);
            }

            ElementId::Ellipse
                if convert_arcs && !self.is_plain_protected(element) && !self.implicated.contains(element) =>
            {
                ConvertShapeToPath::ellipse_to_path(element, path_options, context.info);
            }

            _ => {}
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn has_plain_path_reference<'input>(
    stylesheets: &[std::cell::RefCell<lightningcss::rules::CssRuleList<'input>>],
) -> Result<bool, JobsError<'input>> {
    let mut visitor = HasPlainPath { found: false };
    for stylesheet in stylesheets {
        stylesheet.borrow_mut().0.visit(&mut visitor)?;
    }

/// Merge multiple paths into one
///
/// # Differences to SVGO
///
/// There's no need to specify precision or spacing for path serialization.
///
/// # Correctness
///
/// By default this job should never visually change the document.
///
/// Running with `force` may cause intersecting paths to be incorrectly merged.
///
/// # Errors
///
/// Never.
///
/// If this job produces an error or panic, please raise an [issue](https://github.com/noahbald/oxvg/issues)
pub struct MergePaths {
    #[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", serde(default = "default_force"))]
    /// Whether to merge paths despite intersections
    pub force: bool,
}

impl Default for MergePaths {
    fn default() -> Self {
        MergePaths {
            force: default_force(),
        }
    }
}

impl<'input, 'arena> Visitor<'input, 'arena> for MergePaths {
    type Error = JobsError<'input>;

    fn prepare(
        &self,
        document: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
        context: &mut Context<'input, 'arena, '_>,
    ) -> Result<PrepareOutcome, Self::Error> {
        context.query_has_stylesheet(document);
        Ok(PrepareOutcome::none)
    }

    #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]
    fn element(
        &self,
        element: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
        context: &mut Context<'input, 'arena, '_>,
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let mut children = itertools::peek_nth(element.children_iter());
        if children.peek_nth(1).is_none() {
            return Ok(());
        }

        let mut prev_path_data: Option<path::Path> = None;

        for (prev_child, child) in children.tuple_windows() {
            log::debug!("trying to merge {child:?}");
            macro_rules! update_previous_path {
                ($prev_child:ident) => {
                    if let Some(data) = prev_path_data.take() {
                        set_attribute!(prev_child, D(data));
                    }
                    prev_path_data = None;
                };
            }

            if !is_element!(prev_child, Path)
                || !prev_child.is_empty()
                || has_attribute!(prev_child, Id)
            {
                log::debug!("ending merge, prev not a plain path");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            }

            if !is_element!(child, Path) || !child.is_empty() {
                log::debug!("ending merge, current not a plain path");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            }
            let computed_styles = ComputedStyles::default()
                .with_all(&child, &context.query_has_stylesheet_result)
                .map_err(JobsError::ComputedStylesError)?;
            let Some(mut current_path_data) =
                get_attribute_mut!(child, D).map(|d| RefMut::map(d, |path::Path(d, _)| d))
            else {
                log::debug!("ending merge, current has no `d`");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            };
            if let Some(first) = current_path_data.0.first_mut() {
                if let command::Data::MoveBy(data) = first {
                    *first = command::Data::MoveTo(*data);

                    if let Some(second) = current_path_data.0.get_mut(1) {
                        if second.is_implicit() && second.as_explicit().id() != command::ID::LineTo
                        {
                            *second = second.as_explicit().clone();
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            drop(current_path_data);

            if
                has_computed_style!(
                    computed_styles,
                    MarkerStart | MarkerMid | MarkerEnd | ClipPath | Mask
                )
                || has_computed_style_css!(computed_styles, MaskImage(None))
                || get_computed_style!(computed_styles, Fill).is_some_and(|(fill, mode)| {
                    matches!(mode, Mode::Static)
                        && matches!(fill.option(), Some(SVGPaint::Url { url,.. }) if url.url.starts_with('#'))
                })
                || get_computed_style!(computed_styles, Filter).is_some_and(|(filter, mode)| {
                    matches!(mode, Mode::Static)
                        && matches!(filter, Inheritable::Defined(FilterList::Filters(filters)) if filters.iter().any(|filter| matches!(filter, Filter::Url(url) if url.url.starts_with('#'))))
                })
                || get_computed_style!(computed_styles, Stroke).is_some_and(|(stroke, mode)| {
                    matches!(mode, Mode::Static) && matches!(stroke.option(), Some(SVGPaint::Url { url,.. }) if url.url.starts_with('#'))
                })
            {
                log::debug!("ending merge, has forbidden style or reference");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            }

            let prev_attrs = prev_child.attributes();
            let attrs = child.attributes();
            if prev_attrs.len() != attrs.len() {
                log::debug!("ending merge, current attrs length different to prev");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            }

            let are_any_attr_diff = attrs.into_iter().any(|a| {
                !is_attribute!(a, D) && prev_attrs.get_named_item(a.name()).is_none_or(|p| *p != *a)
            });
            if are_any_attr_diff {
                log::debug!("ending merge, current attrs equal to prev");
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
                continue;
            }

            let has_prev_path = prev_path_data.is_some();
            if prev_path_data.is_none() {
                prev_path_data = get_attribute!(prev_child, D).as_deref().cloned();
            }

            let current_path_data = get_attribute!(child, D)
                .map(|d| cell::Ref::map(d, |path::Path(d, _)| d))
                .expect("D previously used");
            if let Some(path::Path(prev_path_data, _)) = &mut prev_path_data {
                if prev_path_data.0.last().is_some_and(|d| {
                    matches!(
                        d.id().as_explicit(),
                        command::ID::MoveTo | command::ID::MoveBy
                    )
                }) {
                    prev_path_data.0.pop();
                }
                if self.force || !prev_path_data.intersects(&current_path_data) {
                    log::debug!("merging, current doesn't intersect prev");
                    prev_path_data.0.extend(current_path_data.0.clone());
                    prev_child.remove();
                    continue;
                }
            }

            log::debug!("ending merge, current doesn't intersect prev");
            if has_prev_path {
                update_previous_path!(prev_child);
            } else {
                prev_path_data = None;
            }
        }
        if let Some(prev_path_data) = prev_path_data {
            set_attribute!(element.last_element_child().unwrap(), D(prev_path_data));
        }

+fn flatten_would_affect_implicated<'input, 'arena>(
+    element: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
+    implicated: &Implicated<'input, 'arena>,
+) -> bool {
+    if implicated.contains(element) {
+        log::debug!("collapse_groups: not flattening: implicated group");
+        return true;
+    }
+    if element.children_iter().any(|child| implicated.contains(&child)) {
+        log::debug!("collapse_groups: not flattening: implicated child");
+        return true;
+    }
+    // Removing `element` shifts all following siblings, so an implicated
+    // following sibling may stop matching structural pseudo-classes.
+    let mut sibling = element.next_element_sibling();
+    while let Some(s) = sibling {
+        if implicated.contains(&s) {
+            log::debug!("collapse_groups: not flattening: implicated next sibling");
+            return true;
+        }
+        sibling = s.next_element_sibling();
+    }
+    false
+}

+fn removal_would_affect_implicated<'input, 'arena>(
+    element: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
+    implicated: &Implicated<'input, 'arena>,
+) -> bool {
+    if implicated.contains(element) {
+        log::debug!("remove_empty_containers: not removing: implicated element");
+        return true;
+    }
+    if element
+        .parent_element()
+        .is_some_and(|parent| implicated.contains(&parent))
+    {
+        log::debug!("remove_empty_containers: not removing: implicated parent");
+        return true;
+    }
+    let mut sibling = element.next_element_sibling();
+    while let Some(s) = sibling {
+        if implicated.contains(&s) {
+            log::debug!("remove_empty_containers: not removing: implicated following sibling");
+            return true;
+        }
+        sibling = s.next_element_sibling();
+    }
+    false
+}

path to a reusable group, check if it's implicated; if so, don't include it in the group (leave it as path).

Hmm, the reuse_paths snapshot shows BOTH paths converted to `<use>`! The first path (which is `path:first-child` and should be implicated) was NOT
protected. Why?

Because `reuse_paths::State::prepare` collects implicated, but `add_path` is called during `element()` which runs AFTER `prepare`. Wait,
`start_with_context` calls `prepare` then visits elements. So implicated should be set before `add_path`. But the snapshot shows both paths reused.
Let me check: maybe `path:first-child` isn't considered structure-sensitive by our `is_structure_sensitive`? `:first-child` parses as
`Component::Nth(NthSelectorData { ty: Child, a:0, b:1 })` (likely). Our `is_structure_sensitive` checks `Component::Nth(_)` → true. So it should be
structural. Then `Implicated::collect` should find the first path as target.

But wait, `reuse_paths` runs `State::default().start_with_context(document, context)` in `prepare` of the OUTER ReusePaths. The `start_with_context`
calls the State's `prepare` (which queries stylesheet and collects implicated), then visits elements. The `add_path` for each path checks
`self.implicated.borrow().as_ref().is_some_and(...)`. If implicated is set, the first path should be skipped.


both are reused. That's actually correct behavior! My test was wrong - I intended `:first-child` to match the first path but the style element
precedes it.

//! Collects elements whose matching with stylesheet selectors depends on the
//! document structure. Structure-changing rewrites must not touch these
//! elements, otherwise selectors may stop matching (or start matching) where
//! they previously did not.
use std::{cell::RefCell, collections::HashSet};

use lightningcss::{
    printer::PrinterOptions,
    rules::CssRuleList,
    selector::{Combinator, Component, Selector},
    visit_types,
    visitor::{Visit, Visitor},
};
use oxvg_ast::element::{Element, HashableElement};
use oxvg_collections::{attribute::AttrId, element::ElementId};
use oxvg_serialize::ToValue as _;

use crate::error::JobsError;

/// A set of elements that are implicated by structure-sensitive stylesheet
/// selectors.
///
/// An element is implicated by a selector when it is the selector's target, or
/// when it is an anchor in the selector relationship (e.g. the `path` in
/// `path + rect`, or the `g` in `g > rect`). The set is computed from the
/// document before any rewrite so that a rewrite cannot erase the evidence the
/// selector depends on.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Implicated<'input, 'arena> {
    elements: HashSet<HashableElement<'input, 'arena>>,
}

impl<'input, 'arena> Implicated<'input, 'arena> {
    /// Collects all elements implicated by selectors in `stylesheets`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// If a stylesheet cannot be visited.
    pub fn collect(
        root: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
        stylesheets: &[RefCell<CssRuleList<'input>>],
    ) -> Result<Self, JobsError<'input>> {
        let mut collector = Collector {
            root: root.clone(),
            implicated: HashSet::new(),
        };
        for stylesheet in stylesheets {
            stylesheet.borrow_mut().0.visit(&mut collector)?;
        }
        Ok(Self {
            elements: collector.implicated,
        })
    }

    /// Returns whether `element` is implicated by a structure-sensitive
    /// selector.
    pub fn contains(&self, element: &Element<'input, 'arena>) -> bool {
        self.elements.contains(&HashableElement::new(element.clone()))
    }

    /// Collects elements that are targets of plain (non-structure-sensitive)
    /// selectors referencing `local_name`. These elements must not be renamed
    /// away from `local_name`, even though the selector itself does not depend
    /// on document structure.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// If a stylesheet cannot be visited.
    pub fn collect_plain_targets<'a>(
        root: &Element<'input, 'arena>,
        stylesheets: &[RefCell<CssRuleList<'input>>],
        local_name: &'a str,
    ) -> Result<HashSet<HashableElement<'input, 'arena>>, JobsError<'input>> {
        let mut collector = PlainTargetsCollector {
            root: root.clone(),
            local_name,
            targets: HashSet::new(),
        };
        for stylesheet in stylesheets {
            stylesheet.borrow_mut().0.visit(&mut collector)?;
        }
        Ok(collector.targets)
    }
}

struct Collector<'input, 'arena> {
    root: Element<'input, 'arena>,
    implicated: HashSet<HashableElement<'input, 'arena>>,
}

impl<'input, 'arena> Collector<'input, 'arena> {
    fn insert(&mut self, element: &Element<'input, 'arena>) {
        self.implicated.insert(HashableElement::new(element.clone()));
    }

    fn process_selector(&mut self, selector: &Selector<'input>) {
        // Split the selector into compounds (left to right) and the combinators
        // connecting them. `iter_raw_match_order` yields the components in
        // right-to-left order, so reversing the split gives parse order.
        let mut compounds: Vec<Vec<Component<'input>>> = Vec::new();
        let mut combinators: Vec<Combinator> = Vec::new();
        let mut current: Vec<Component<'input>> = Vec::new();
        for component in selector.iter_raw_match_order().cloned() {
            match component {
                Component::Combinator(combinator) => {
                    combinators.push(combinator);
                    compounds.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
                }
                component => current.push(component),
            }
        }
        compounds.push(current);
        compounds.reverse();
        combinators.reverse();

        if compounds.is_empty() || !is_structure_sensitive(selector) {
            return;
        }

        // Find the selector's targets in the pre-rewrite document by matching
        // manually. This is needed because the `selectors` crate used by
        // `root.select` does not support `:has` and some structural

MESSAGE
I've implemented the fix and committed everything on a new branch `fix/structure-sensitive-selectors`.

## Summary

The problem was that structure-changing optimisations could break (or newly create) stylesheet matches for selectors that depend on document
structure, and the existing protection was either missing or too coarse (e.g. `convertShapeToPath` skipped the whole job whenever any selector
mentioned `path`).

### What I did

1. **Added a new `Implicated` utility** (`crates/oxvg_optimiser/src/utils/implicated.rs`):
   - Scans all stylesheet selectors before any rewrite.
   - For each structure-sensitive selector (combinators, `:has`, `:nth-*`, `:empty`, etc.), it manually matches the pre-rewrite DOM and collects both
**selector targets** and **anchor elements** (e.g. the `rect` in `rect + path`, or the `g` in `g > rect`).
   - This makes protection precise: only the specific element/relationship actually implicated is protected; unrelated elements remain optimisable.
   - It also provides `collect_plain_targets` for `convertShapeToPath` so plain selectors like `rect` still protect the specific shapes they
reference.

2. **Wired the protection into structure-changing jobs**:
   - `collapse_groups` — avoids flattening a group when it, its children, or following siblings are implicated.
   - `remove_empty_containers` — avoids removing implicated containers.
   - `convert_shape_to_path` — only skips converting implicated shapes; preserves the old conservative behaviour when a plain `path` selector is
present.
   - `merge_paths` — avoids merging implicated paths.
   - `reuse_paths` — avoids reusing implicated paths.

3. **Added snapshot tests** covering:
   - `g:has(> path)` and `svg > g > path` in `collapseGroups`.
   - `path + rect` (target) and `rect + path` (anchor) in `convertShapeToPath`.
   - plain `path` selector still disables conversion.
   - `path + path` in `mergePaths` and `path:nth-child(2)` in `reusePaths`.

All workspace tests pass (65 optimiser tests + all other crates), and the working tree is clean on the new branch.
